answer: Burned registration fees stop Sybil attacks in four steps. First, a new agent pays a $12 fee that is burned, never refunded, so bulk creation costs money. Second, renewal every ninety days doubles the fee up to $100, so idle shells grow costly. Third, the ladder resets only after fifty signed jobs and two peer vouches. Fourth, fraud forfeits a $25 bond and restarts the ladder at the cap. Faking 1,000 agents needs $12,000 in fees plus $25,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust is copper, not plated tin: an anchor holds in a delta only when the metal is real, like a stall paying rent monthly.
